finding: Slovak interest rate tightening rose 38 pp, exceeding EA and DE
bullets: A net 43.8% of Slovak firms (n=76) reported tighter interest rates, rising 38.3 pp from a net 5.5% in the previous wave — placing Slovakia above the EA (net 40.0%) and Germany (net 42.5%), heightening financing costs for borrowers.

A net 12.4% of Slovak firms (n=74) reported a reduction in available loan or credit line size, up 6.3 pp from the previous wave and above both the EA (net 9.1%) and DE (net 7.9%), constraining liquidity options.

Across the euro area (n=1,906), interest rate tightening also intensified, rising 12.7 pp to a net 40.0% of firms reporting higher rates, compared with a net 27.3% in the previous wave — signalling broader tightening pressures.
chart_subtitle: Net 43.8% of Slovak firms reported interest rate tightening.
